$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}, & -1\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=0.6,$ calculate $P(0<\overset{―}{X}<0.2).$

*Hint: Assume that the sample size is sufficiently large for the central limit theorem to be applied. A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8643\,$ | $\,0.8665\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ | $\,0.8729\,$ | $\,0.8749\,$ |

questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =20,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}x\cdot \frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{3}{2}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3{x}^{4}}{8}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=0.6.$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(0,\frac{0.6}{20}) \\  & ∼N(0,0.03).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(0<\overset{―}{X}<0.2).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<\overset{―}{X}<0.2) & =P(\frac{0-0}{\sqrt{0.03}}<Z<\frac{0.2-0}{\sqrt{0.03}}) \\  & ≈P(0<Z<1.15) \\  & =P(Z<1.15)-P(Z<0) \\  & =Φ(1.15)-Φ(0).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have that

$$
Φ(1.15)=0.8749,
$$

and by the symmetry of the normal distribution, $Φ(0)=0.5.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<\overset{―}{X}<0.2) & =Φ(1.15)-Φ(0) \\  & =0.8749-0.5 \\  & =0.3749\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =25,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}x\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{3}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =2.5,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=0.75.$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(2.5,\frac{0.75}{25}) \\  & ∼N(2.5,0.03).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(2.4<\overset{―}{X}<2.7).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2.4<\overset{―}{X}<2.7) & =P(\frac{2.4-2.5}{\sqrt{0.03}}<Z<\frac{2.7-2.5}{\sqrt{0.03}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.58<Z<1.15) \\  & =P(Z<1.15)-P(Z<-0.58) \\  & =Φ(1.15)-Φ(-0.58)\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.15) & =0.8749, \\ Φ(-0.58) & =0.2810.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2.4<\overset{―}{X}<2.7) & =Φ(1.15)-Φ(-0.58) \\  & =0.8749-0.2810 \\  & =0.5939.\end{aligned}
$$

Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =20,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{4} \\  & =0.75,\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(0.75,\frac{0.04}{20}) \\  & ∼N(0.75,0.002).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<0.8) & =P(Z<\frac{0.8-0.75}{\sqrt{0.002}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<1.12) \\  & =Φ(1.12)\end{aligned}

Φ(1.12)=0.8686.

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<0.8) & =Φ(1.12) \\  & =0.8686.\end{aligned}
$$

Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
n=47,
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =1\cdot 0.4+2\cdot 0.35+4\cdot 0.1+10\cdot 0.15 \\  & =0.4+0.7+0.4+1.5 \\  & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =({1}^{2}\cdot 0.4+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.35+{4}^{2}\cdot 0.1+{10}^{2}\cdot 0.15)-{3}^{2} \\  & =(0.4+1.4+1.6+15)-9 \\  & =9.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(3,\frac{9.4}{47}) \\  & ∼N(3,0.2).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>3.2).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>3.2) & ≈P(Z>\frac{3.2-3}{\sqrt{0.2}}) \\  & =P(Z>0.45) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.45) \\  & =1-Φ(0.45).\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.45)=0.6736.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>3.2) & =1-Φ(0.45) \\  & =1-0.6736 \\  & =0.3264.\end{aligned}
$$
